title: Reset all settings in a dconf directory
summary: Reset all configuration keys within a specific dconf directory to their default values. This is useful when you want to revert a whole section of settings (like GNOME Shell extensions or specific app configs) without affecting others.

aliases.text: reset all dconf settings in folder

steps.explain: Use the -f flag to reset all keys under the specified directory path. Ensure the path ends with a slash.

placeholders.name: DIRECTORY_PATH
placeholders.description: The dconf directory path to reset, e.g., /org/gnome/desktop/

warnings: This will permanently delete all custom settings in the specified directory and its subdirectories.
You cannot undo this action unless you have a backup of your dconf database.

rollback.explain: There is no direct command to restore previous values. You must manually re-apply your settings or restore from a backup if you have one.
